Once upon a time...

Once, in a distant land. There lived a weary knight.

He carried deep wounds within him, carrying the weight of years of exhaustion silently within his heart.
He had grown accustomed to struggling against everything and everyone.
Whenever he fell, he rose again. Whenever he was hurt, he hid his wounds beneath his armor.
He believed himself invincible, unbreakable, untouchable.

And yet, from every battle he entered, he emerged a little more broken.
His body carried the scars left by countless blades, while his mind carried wounds no one could ever see.

And among all those battles, the knight had one fear he never spoke of.
Losing his delicate rose.
The one thing he cherished above all else. The one thing he wished to return to after every battle.
The knight wanted to protect her.
From the harshness of the world, from the storms, from the thorns, from all the darkness that surrounded them...
But there was something he did not understand. Sometimes, a person can hurt the very thing they are trying to protect, simply because of the wounds they carry themselves.
The knight did not know this.
He never saw the marks he was leaving upon her petals. He never realized how heavy his own hands had become.

Until one day...
He saw that his rose was wounded.
In that moment, time itself seemed to stop. His armor suddenly became unbearably heavy. Heavier than all the iron he had carried all those years...
He was rendered speechless.
His sword slipped from his hand.
And for the first time in his life, a fear he had never known—not even on the bloodiest battlefield—crept into his very bones.
Because this time he wasnt standing before an army, a dragon, or a monster.

The knight did not know what to do.
He had spent years fighting.
He had spent years tending to his own wounds. Whenever he fell, he had always been the one to pull himself back to his feet.
But this time, there was nothing he could fight. Because for the first time, there was something he was truly afraid to lose.

He looked at his rose.
And tears began to fall from his eyes.
But these were not ordinary tears.
They carried the color of all the fear, regret, and pain he had buried inside himself for so many years.

They were the tears of blood.

The knight looked down at his hands.
Those hands had won countless battles.
They had struck down countless enemies.
They had tended to countless wounds.
But now, for the first time, he was afraid of his own hands.

Because in that moment, he finally understood, a person can learn how to fight against the whole world, but learning how not to hurt the one they love is an entirely different battle.

And for the first time, the knight fell to his knees.
He lowered his head toward his rose.
He did not know what to say. He wanted to apologize, but the words were tangled in his throat. Because some wounds are too deep for any words to be enough.
That night, the knight realized that he had finally been defeated. But this defeat was unlike all the others he had known. This time, he had not been defeated by the world. He had been defeated by himself.

And perhaps...
For the first time in his life, he understood that the battle he truly needed to fight was not outside of him, but within.

text:
He wore iron armor, scarred and cold,
A sworn protector, fierce and bold.
She wore silk gowns, a royal crown,
A princess locked in a golden town.
He stood at the door where the shadows fell,
Guarding a secret he'd never tell.
She glanced through the archway, catching his eye,
A silent nod as she drifted by.
He was the sword that kept danger away,
She was the dawn of a forbidden day.
A knight shouldn't look at the royal blood,
A princess shouldn't dream in the mud.
He held his breath when she touched his shield,
A battlefield where his heart would yield.
She whispered a word when no one was near,
And chased away every lingering fear.
The kingdom demanded a matching throne,
While he was a soldier, standing alone.
No titles, no lands, just a heavy blade,
And a love in the dark that would never fade.
When danger arrived and the castle shook,
He fought for her life with a desperate look.
Bleeding and weary, he stood in the light,
To guide her safe through the darkest night.
She tore her own veil to bind up his scar,
Wished he could ride with her past the far star.
No crown could ever replace his embrace,
No throne could rival his humble face.
They never spoke of the vows unsaid,
With heavy hearts and a quiet tread.
He stayed by the gates as the carriage rolled,
A story of silver, a romance of gold.
Some hearts are bound by a wall of stone,
Destined to love, but to walk alone.
